subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Invention of the Airbag
description: One-minute skill: The Invention of the Airbag.

hook.text: In 1953, a retired engineer named John Hetrick patented an inflatable crash cushion.

buildup.text: His idea sat unused for nearly two decades because no one could inflate a bag fast enough.

discovery.text: By the 1970s, chemical propellants could fill an airbag with gas in just 30 milliseconds.

twist.text: Ford and GM tested early airbags, but abandoned them because some deployed randomly.

climax.text: Mercedes became the first to offer a driver airbag in 1981, proving the concept worked safely.

punchline.text: It took 28 years to make a split-second idea work.

quiz.question: Why were airbags delayed for decades after their invention?
options: Nobody could inflate them fast enough

details.summary: Airbags deploy from the steering wheel and dashboard in milliseconds during a crash, creating a cushion that decelerates the occupant's head and torso more gently than hitting a hard surface.
details.whyItMatters: Combined with seatbelts, frontal airbags reduce driver fatality risk by about 30 percent. Their widespread adoption since the 1990s has saved tens of thousands of lives worldwide.
takeaways: Airbags inflate in roughly 30 milliseconds using a gas generator
They work best in combination with seatbelts, not as replacements
Modern cars may contain more than ten airbags in various locations

faq.question: Can airbags injure occupants when they deploy?
faq.answer: Yes. Airbags deploy with great force and can cause burns, abrasions, or injuries to unbelted or improperly positioned occupants. This is why seatbelts are essential to keep occupants in the correct position.

faq.question: Who invented the automotive airbag?
faq.answer: American engineer John Hetrick patented an early airbag concept in 1953. The first production airbags appeared in some GM and Ford vehicles in the 1970s, but widespread adoption came in the 1990s.
